newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Seven buyers said interested in Sweden's Enator.
newsitem.headline: Seven buyers said interested in Sweden's Enator.

text.p: Seven Swedish and overseas companies have expressed interest in buying the state's 25 percent holding of data company Enator, Swedish business newspaper Dagens Industri said on Saturday.
The state's slice, which is the largest single holding in the computer company and worth an estimated 1.4 billion crowns, is expected to be sold in the next three months.
"I estimate that there are seven serious possible buyers," government spokesman Per Tegner, who is handling the sale for the business department, told Dagens Industri.

Enator's deputy managing director Jerry Lundqvist has already said that an international accountancy firm, that owns IT interests, would be a good strategic partner for Enator which is the largest data company on the Stockholm bourse.

The newspaper said another potential buyer would be a big telecommunications operator that was already present in Sweden as Enator owns an old local government data network with 66,000 users spread throughout the public sector.
It said Telenordia along with British Telecom, Telenor and Tele Danmark were the most likely contenders.
Even the Global One consortium, grouping France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp, was a possibility, said Dagens Industri.
"I know the business department has been in contact with France Telecom over this matter," Global One Sweden's managing director Lars Persson told the paper.
Another possible buyer was seen to be the data consultancy company Computer Science Corp that wants to establish an IT company with Volvo Data.
